questions.stem: Scenario S5, Claude Code for continuous integration. A team runs Claude Code in CI to review pull requests. The labels for how bad a finding is are free text, and the gate cannot compare them with its floor. Which change fixes it?

options.text: Ask for stronger adjectives on urgent findings
options.says: Ruled out because "A definition with a code example gives the reviewer a case to compare with", and adjectives give none.

options.text: Let the gate guess each level from the issue's words
options.says: Ruled out because the gate needs a value it can compute with: "an open, free-text severity cannot be computed with".

options.text: Close the field to a fixed list, with a sample per level
options.says: A level with a code sample has a boundary, and a closed list can be compared with a floor.

options.text: Drop the floor and accept every label as written
options.says: Ruled out because the gate "drops findings below a floor and fails the job at a severity", and without a floor it has no policy.

questions.stem: Scenario S5, Claude Code for continuous integration. A team runs Claude Code in CI to review pull requests. One group of findings has 40 percent precision. Its dismissals all trace to line-length remarks, while its other remarks are always accepted. What fits?

options.text: Disable the whole group until every remark in it improves
options.says: Ruled out because "The fix is then to adjust the criteria for the one pattern and not to disable the category".

options.text: Adjust the criteria for that one pattern
options.says: The recorded pattern shows where the dismissals come from, so only that part is adjusted.

options.text: Delete the group's criteria and start over with none
options.says: Ruled out because "Deleting the category from the criteria loses the examples that the next attempt needs".

options.text: Leave the group unchanged while more reviews accumulate
options.says: Ruled out because leaving the group unchanged keeps the noise, which has a cost, since "each dismissed comment lowers trust in the accepted ones".

origin.section: Record the pattern behind each finding

questions.stem: Scenario S5, Claude Code for continuous integration. A team runs Claude Code in CI to review pull requests. A review run starts from a request whose branch name is blank, and the project defines `main` as the default. What should it do?

options.text: Ask the author which branch is meant, then wait
options.says: Ruled out because "Asking in CI produces a job that waits for a person who is not there".

options.text: Stop with a failure naming the required field
options.says: Ruled out because it stops only without a default: "it proceeds on stated assumptions where a default exists".

options.text: Continue with the fallback and note it in the output
options.says: A run that cannot ask proceeds on a stated assumption where a default exists.

options.text: Choose a branch at random and leave it unmentioned
options.says: Ruled out because a silent guess omits the step the page requires, which is "to state the assumptions made for the rest".
